part5.question: Delegates attending the international trade convention were provided with overnight ------- at Hotel Boswick.
part5.explanation: After the preposition "with" and adjective "overnight," a noun is needed to complete the object phrase; "accommodations" (lodging) fits both grammatically and semantically, unlike the verb and participle forms (A)-(C).

part5.question: Charles Wang submitted a resume that ------- his years of experience in advertising.
part5.explanation: The verb "emphasized" (highlighted) best describes what a resume does to showcase work experience, whereas "enclosed" (placed inside), "estimated" (approximated), and "employed" (hired/used) do not fit the context.

part5.question: Beginning next week, Zumwalt, Inc.'s new smartphone will be available for purchase at ------- retailers across Korea and Japan.
part5.explanation: Before the plural noun "retailers," the past-participle adjective "authorized" (officially approved to sell products) is required rather than the active participle "authorizing" (A) or the nouns "authority" (B) and "authorization" (C).

part5.question: Highway construction has been postponed indefinitely as Hampshire County residents have ------- to the plan.
part5.explanation: "Objections" (opposition/complaints) pairs naturally with "to the plan" and explains why highway construction was postponed indefinitely, unlike "preferences," "arrangements," or "considerations."

part5.question: The Trescott Chamber of Commerce ------- local businessman Brian Larue at a ceremony next week.
part5.explanation: The future time marker "next week" calls for the future tense verb "will honor" (C); (A) is past progressive, (B) is an infinitive lacking a main verb, and (D) is a bare/plural verb incompatible with the singular subject.

part5.question: Please review your contract, and feel free to ask us ------- questions you might have.
part5.explanation: The determiner "any" properly modifies the plural noun "questions" in an open invitation ("ask us any questions you might have"), whereas "few" implies almost none, "either" takes a singular noun, and "much" requires an uncountable noun.

part5.question: The manager announced that a few office supply ------- would be delayed because of weather conditions.
part5.explanation: The quantifier "a few" must modify a plural countable noun, making "shipments" (B) the only grammatically valid choice.

part5.question: By adding extra flights between Dubai and Istanbul, Euroblue Airlines will increase its ------- for this route by more than 50 percent.
part5.explanation: Adding extra flights increases an airline's passenger or cargo "capacity" (carrying volume) on a route, whereas "endurance," "motivation," and "location" do not fit.

part5.question: Halmilton Hospital's purchase of a medical scanning device will permit doctors to diagnose patients more ------- than ever before.
part5.explanation: An adverb is required to modify the verb "diagnose," making "precisely" (forming the comparative "more precisely") correct instead of the adjective "precise" (A) or nouns "precision" (C) and "preciseness" (D).

part5.question: ------- a bank has approved Flynn Co.'s business loan, the company can begin its planned expansion.
part5.explanation: The subordinating conjunction "Now that" (meaning "because a new situation is true") links the loan approval to the company's ability to expand, whereas "Even if" and "As though" carry the wrong meaning and "Consequently" cannot join two clauses here.

part5.question: Online reviewers praise Alpha Fashion's ------- deliveries and its generous return policy.
part5.explanation: The adjective "timely" (prompt/on time) logically describes deliveries that customers praise, unlike "tangible" (touchable), "measured" (deliberate/slow), or "subsequent" (following).

part5.question: Though Bruce Guthrie's concert is planned ------- August 1, the organizers have said that this is subject to change.
part5.explanation: The verb phrase "is planned for [a date]" uses the preposition "for" to indicate the scheduled date of an event, whereas "at," "since," and "in" do not collocate with "planned" before a specific calendar date.

part5.question: The public speaking course presents trainees with opportunities ------- themselves in front of a group.
part5.explanation: The to-infinitive "to express" properly modifies the noun "opportunities" to express purpose, whereas finite verb forms (A, C) and the past tense/participle "expressed" (D) are ungrammatical in this slot.

part5.question: The speaker at the Westicon Literature Seminar told an ------- story that had the entire audience laughing in enjoyment.
part5.explanation: A participial adjective describing a thing that causes laughter ("story") uses the -ing form "amusing" (entertaining), whereas "amused" (C) describes a person's reaction and (B) and (D) are noun/verb forms.

part5.question: A fee of $100 will be ------- to office rental payments that are more than two weeks late.
part5.explanation: Following the passive auxiliary "will be," the past participle "applied" is needed to form the passive verb phrase "will be applied to" (charged to).

part5.question: Last month's issue of Wise Finance ------- an exclusive interview with Chuck Granville, founder of financial firm Granville Investments.
part5.explanation: The verb "featured" (included as a prominent highlight) fits an issue of a magazine containing an exclusive interview, unlike "subscribed," "admitted," or "dedicated."

part5.question: Broadcasting the ------- latest news 24 hours a day, cable station CPP allows viewers to keep up-to-date on world events.
part5.explanation: The adverb "very" idiomatically intensifies the superlative adjective "latest" in the phrase "the very latest news," whereas "fewer," "far," and "more" cannot stand between "the" and "latest."

part5.question: The software ------- that New-Tech offers remove security risks and improve the performance of computers.
part5.explanation: Software "enhancements" (upgrades/improvements) logically remove security risks and boost computer performance, whereas "increments," "certificates," and "exceptions" do not fit.

part5.question: Mr. Evans took a taxi to avoid being late, but the theater show had ------- begun by the time he arrived.
part5.explanation: The adverb "already" fits the past perfect "had already begun" to indicate the show started before Mr. Evans arrived, while frequency adverbs like "usually," "seldom," and "hourly" conflict with a single completed event.

part5.question: Notices ------- residents of possible power outages were mailed out a week before crews began work on the power lines.
part5.explanation: Because the main verb is "were mailed out," the blank requires the present-participle modifier "informing" (reduced from "which informed") to actively take the direct object "residents."

part5.question: Mr. Clemon's work was so impressive that he was made a senior manager ------- only six months with the company.
part5.explanation: The preposition "after" indicates the time elapsed before his promotion ("after only six months with the company"), whereas "on" and "owing to" have the wrong meaning and "while" requires a clause or participle.

part5.question: In anticipation of an increase in visitors during the summer holiday, the Shoreline Inn decided to ------- hire additional housekeeping staff.
part5.explanation: Hiring extra housekeeping staff specifically for the summer holiday rush calls for the adverb "temporarily" (for a limited time), rather than "adversely," "uncontrollably," or "relatively."

part5.question: Although a graduate degree is a requirement for the position, none of ------- who responded to the job announcement have one.
part5.explanation: After the preposition "of" and before the relative clause "who responded...," the demonstrative pronoun "those" is used idiomatically to mean "the people who."

part5.question: Travel writer Arthur Chaplin will give a short presentation tomorrow ------- the trip he described in his new book, Walking in Peru.
part5.explanation: The preposition "regarding" (about/concerning) introduces the subject of the presentation, whereas "along," "in exchange for," and "by means of" do not fit semantically.

part5.question: Having written multiple books on the effects of global warming, Ms. Black is widely regarded as a ------- expert on environmental issues.
part5.explanation: Having written multiple books establishes Ms. Black as a "notable" (well-known and respected) expert, in contrast to "naive" (inexperienced), "tolerant," or "mundane" (ordinary).

part5.question: Local water quality is ------- to improve once the sewage treatment center is upgraded.
part5.explanation: The expression "be bound to + verb" means "be certain or very likely to happen," making "bound" (C) fit both the structure "is ___ to improve" and the meaning.

part5.question: Charles Kapoor was not considered a suitable candidate for a financial analyst position ------- he possessed exceptional investment experience.
part5.explanation: The subordinating conjunction "even though" connects the contrasting full clause "he possessed exceptional investment experience," whereas "in spite of" (B) is a preposition requiring a noun phrase.

part5.question: The tour bus did not stop at Sheffield Stadium, so its passengers could only take pictures as they drove ------- it.
part5.explanation: Because the tour bus did not stop at the stadium, passengers could only take photos as they drove "past" it (moving alongside and beyond it), unlike "until," "onto," or "within."

part5.question: Mercer Incorporated carefully goes over ------- its customer surveys and market research before making important decisions.
part5.explanation: The correlative conjunction "both" pairs with "and" ("both its customer surveys and market research"), whereas "neither" pairs with "nor" and the other options cannot form this parallel pair.

part5.question: For the purpose of increasing sales, Mendelbaum Electronics is giving a prize to ------- is the 100th person to buy a refrigerator.
part5.explanation: The compound relative pronoun "whoever" functions simultaneously as the object of the preposition "to" and the subject of "is the 100th person," referring to whichever unspecified buyer qualifies.

passages.content:
By Adriana Solo

In recent years, mobile applications and Web sites have made it easier and cheaper for people to do things like get a ride, find a place to stay, or arrange a babysitter. Referred to as "the sharing economy," this new Internet-dependent system brings more wage-earning opportunities to a wider range of people. However, as the practice of purchasing services from individual people rather than conventional businesses grows in popularity, some municipalities have opted to regulate it, or even ban it outright.

Ghorinburg, for instance, has emerged as a strong opponent of the sharing economy and the local government has prohibited residents from participating in it. Mayor of the city, Robert Smollet, who became mayor last year in a landslide victory, says that its advantages are not as great as they seem on the surface. "When you can hire someone to work on a freelance basis for a lower rate, why bother going to a company that will charge much more? Ultimately, the sharing economy can cause businesses to close and the people who work for them to lose their jobs."

Ghorinburg does not stand alone, as other municipalities across the nation are following suit. In smaller cities, like Browenville, Marog, and Quentintown, where local businesses play a vital role in the growth of the economy, restrictions have likewise been adopted. Only time will tell whether attitudes remain this way, as technology is certain to spread to even more aspects of our lives.

*Health Note* — March

**The Truth About Supplements?** *(continued from page 19)*

So, ideally, maintaining a varied diet is enough to satisfy the nutritional requirements of adults aged 65 and older. However, some seniors may find this difficult to do, as they lack time and find preparing nutritious meals to be too challenging. In such cases, many doctors agree that taking vitamins and other supplements may be helpful. Even so, physicians believe that these supplements should be carefully regulated so as not to cause unintended harm. According to a controlled study¹ by the Research Institute for Aging, some vitamins and minerals can be toxic when ingested in large amounts. For this reason, getting the advice of a trusted and qualified physician before beginning a vitamin regimen is recommended.
